fixer.title: Avoid unnecessary --numstat diff for incoming changes decorations

introducer.title: Git - get the diff and num stats for a commit

cases.mechanism: The automatic incoming-decoration refresh eagerly requested insertion/deletion statistics for every changed path even though the only consumer discarded those fields. --numstat requires content comparison and can hydrate missing blobs in partial or virtualized repositories, so the cost scales with the incoming changed-file/content set and can overlap across refreshes.
cases.symptom: Incoming-decoration refreshes on large partial-clone or virtualized repositories could spend 60-200+ seconds and fetch thousands of objects solely for unused numstat data, delaying decoration updates and consuming network/disk I/O.
cases.fixedBehavior: Changed line 261 calls diffBetween, whose no-path implementation executes git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=ADMR for the same triple-dot range. This preserves the Change[] metadata needed by decorations while removing --numstat output, its parser allocations, and eager per-file content/stat work.
cases.evidence: Base line 261 called Repository.diffBetweenWithStats from GitIncomingChangesFileDecorationProvider.getIncomingChanges. That wrapper invokes git diff with --raw --numstat and parses insertion/deletion maps, while collectIncomingChangesFileDecorations consumes only status, uri, and originalUri. The provider runs initially when enabled and on current-history-ref changes after write operations; reported measurements for large partial-clone/VFS ranges are 60-200+ seconds and thousands of hydrated objects. Blame attributes the base line to c95739960ff4c35dd0bf89ef8a8812eb377d7dfc.
